text.p: Attorney-General Khaled al-Kidra said on Thursday he had quit his job in President Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority for health reasons.
The official Palestinian news agency WAFA said Kidra, 62, handed in his resignation to Arafat on Wednesday night and the president accepted it.
The news agency gave no reason for the resignation. But Kidra said he had grown tired from the extensive work demanded by the job.
"There's no reason except for health reasons," he told Reuters.
He denied a report by Israel Radio that the resignation was linked to a recent report by an auditing office set up by Arafat on corruption by officials in Arafat's administration.
"The auditing report has nothing to do at all with the legal apparatus, and the report is totally incorrect," Kidra said.
Kidra, a lawyer in Gaza, was appointed attorney-general after Arafat returned home under a 1993 self-rule deal with Israel.
